basis.governing_question: How should Seguros Atlântida redesign how its claims department is organized, roles and handoffs included?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Map claims work, roles and handoffs as they run today and agree design criteria with the client's leaders.

gate.label: Design scope decision
gate.decision: Which problem areas and design criteria does the Design phase take forward?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the target claims organization (structure, roles, handoffs, transition) and take it to the executive committee for approval.

gate.label: Executive approval
gate.decision: Does the executive committee approve the target claims organization?

workstreams.name: Current-state mapping
workstreams.answers: How is the claims department organized today, in structure, roles and handoffs?
activities: Walk through claims processes and handoffs with the teams
Interview the people who do the claims work in each role
Collect operational data on claims workload and cost

workstreams.name: Leadership needs
workstreams.answers: What do the COO and Head of Claims need the new organization to fix and keep?
activities: Ask the COO and Head of Claims what to fix and keep
Establish with the COO how the executive committee decides
Identify the evidence the committee needs to approve

workstreams.name: Problem areas and criteria
workstreams.answers: Which problem areas and design criteria should the Design phase take forward?
activities: Rank problem areas from the mapping and interviews
Draft design criteria with the COO and Head of Claims
Prepare the Design scope proposal for the gate

workstreams.name: Claims organization options
workstreams.answers: Which options for claims structure, roles and handoffs should be compared, and against which criteria?
activities: Develop options for claims structure, roles and handoffs
Compare the options against the agreed design criteria
Prepare the options for choice at the design workshop

workstreams.name: Target organization design
workstreams.answers: What does the chosen target organization look like in structure, roles, handoffs and governance?
activities: Detail the chosen option's structure, roles and governance
Design handoffs between claims roles and teams
Detail each unit's design with its leaders in two rounds

workstreams.name: Transition plan
workstreams.answers: What transition does the target organization need?
activities: Sequence the steps to reach the target organization
List the role, handoff and governance changes by team
Plan the change support the claims teams will need

workstreams.name: Executive approval
workstreams.answers: What must the executive committee see to approve the target claims organization?
activities: Run the client review and sign-off cycle on the design
Build the pre-read on the evidence the committee asked for
Take the target organization to the executive committee

deliverables.name: Claims baseline: structure, roles, handoffs, workload, cost
Leadership needs and committee approval requirements
Design scope proposal: problem areas and design criteria
Claims organization options compared to design criteria
Detailed design of the target claims organization
Transition roadmap and change plan for claims teams
Executive committee pre-read on the target organization

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the diagnostic and secure access
events.decision: Which claims data and staff will the steering group make available for mapping?
agenda: Present the Diagnostic scope and the weeks 1-3 mapping approach
Align on the data and people the current-state mapping needs
Confirm the interview and data request calendar

events.label: Check-in: first findings
events.decision: Which committee approval requirements must the design criteria be built to meet?
agenda: Present the claims baseline: structure, roles, handoffs
Review leadership needs and committee approval requirements
Discuss how the weeks 4-5 scoping will use these findings

events.label: Design scope decision
events.purpose: Close Diagnostic and set the Design scope
events.decision: Which problem areas and design criteria does the Design phase take forward?
agenda: Present the design scope proposal: problem areas and criteria
Review the baseline and needs behind the proposal
Decide the problem areas and criteria for the Design phase

events.label: Workshop 1: claims options
events.decision: Which claims organization option goes forward into detailed design?
agenda: Present the claims organization options and how they were compared
Review how each option meets the agreed design criteria
Decide which option goes into detailed design

events.label: Workshop 2: target design
events.decision: Does the detailed design go into transition planning and the committee pre-read?
agenda: Present the detailed design: structure, roles, handoffs
Review the design against the agreed design criteria
Decide whether the design moves into transition planning

events.label: Executive approval
events.purpose: Close Design and seek executive approval
events.decision: Does the executive committee approve the target claims organization?
agenda: Present the executive committee pre-read on the target organization
Review the detailed design and the transition roadmap
Decide whether the executive committee approves the design

architect_notes: Engagement length is open: 17-20 weeks is an estimate; slow committee scheduling or a larger target model would push Design to its 17-week top.
Executive committee approval is sized as 1-2 weeks closing Design; if its meeting falls after week 20, the plan ends before the decision.
Four claims teams are assumed; please confirm the count, as unit-level design takes 2-4 weeks and that piece drops if there are none.
The one claims department of about 140 people comes from public research and needs the client's confirmation, as it sets the Diagnostic length.
The executive committee must approve the target organization but is not among the stated stakeholders; confirm who represents it at the final gate.

sub_questions.question: How is the claims department organized today, in structure, roles and handoffs?
What do the Chief Operating Officer and Head of Claims need the new organization to fix and keep?
Which options for the claims structure, roles and handoffs should be compared, and against which criteria?
What does the chosen target organization look like in structure, roles, handoffs and governance?
What transition does the target organization need, and what must the executive committee see to approve it?

drivers.evidence: One claims department of about 140 people in Lisbon.

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Unit diagnosed (interviews, process walk-throughs, workload and cost baseline)

phases.why: One department diagnosed in one pass; interviews and process walk-throughs run together.

phases.name: Design

work.unit: Target model for the whole organization (structure, roles, governance)
Unit-level design detailed with the unit's leaders
Executive committee pre-read, review and approval

phases.why: Sequential; unit-level design runs in two rounds of two teams. Extra rounds and two approvals lift the top above the typical 10 weeks.

sizing.levers: Running unit-level design and the transition plan side by side, or comparing fewer target model options, would shorten Design most.
